findings.text: assert pulse.id == "demo:codac_uda:slow:DEMO:CAMPAIGN/commissioning-alpha" compares the constructor's output against the same literal the test handed in as id= on line 99, so it stays green for any implementation that derives the ID from archive and name, including one with the supplied-ID check deleted at imas_codex/config/codac_uda.py:63. It guards derivation, not the accept arm its name claims; the refusal arm is independently guarded by test_pulse_construction_refuses_mismatched_id and its mutation receipt.

create_archive_pulse has no production call site anywhere under imas_codex/ (only tests/graph/test_archive_schema.py imports it), and direct Pulse construction still accepts a truncated ID because the generated model at imas_codex/graph/models.py:15138 carries no cross-field rule. The enforcement is therefore opt-in and prospective: a scanner that constructs Pulse directly can still write the colliding ID the repair exists to prevent. The docstring and the evidence fragment state this limitation honestly.
